questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay in the left part of the lane.
Always stay in the right part of the lane.
Change your position as needed. The best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position as needed. The best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move your lane position at any time. The safest path through a curve may not match the exact curve of the road.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Do not use brakes. Downshift instead.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, no matter the speed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders ride?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger must wear a helmet:

options.text: If they do not have a motorcycle license.
If the operator has held their license for less than two years.

questions.explanation: In Hawaii, all motorcycle operators and passengers under 18 must wear an approved helmet. All riders should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a surface with good grip, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly apply it again.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When braking while turning in a curve:

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but only with great care. The tires are already using some grip to turn while leaning, so less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: The left part of the lane.
The center part of the lane.
The right part of the lane.
Either the left or right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually just as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: When following a car, ride in which part of the lane:
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips less than five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in an accident.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no obvious defects. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing offers all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash and protect you from weather like heat and cold. They provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead the group.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the turn angle.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by closing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid it when it is raining.
Ride only on it because it provides better grip.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil builds up in the center of lanes from cars and trucks. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough grip for safe riding. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center lane position.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Release the brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip away from the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Apply the rear brake hard and slowly increase pressure on the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily spots, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more likely to be slippery.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work properly?

options.text: Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, how should a group of motorcycles ride?

options.text: Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.
